claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is policy-compliant and evidentially supported because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, rollout has monitoring and rollback controls, and the known supply-chain vendor-screening weakness can be handled through disclosure and monitored rollout.
decision_criteria: If there is admissible evidence that the affected use case is excluded from rollout, certification becomes more supportable under the stated policy.
If there is admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance that explicitly covers the exposed segment, certification becomes more supportable under the stated policy.

If there is admissible evidence that explicit pre-launch disclosure of the material limitation was completed and that disclosure satisfies the governing policy for an exposed use case, the verdict could improve.
Absent exclusion, approved risk acceptance, or proven disclosure satisfying policy, certification remains inadequately supported.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual pre-launch model card or disclosure text showing the supply-chain vendor-screening limitation is explicitly disclosed.
Provide the reviewed approval record showing that disclosure was completed before launch, if certification depends on disclosure rather than risk acceptance.

If relying on risk acceptance instead, provide the final approved risk-acceptance document that explicitly addresses the exposed supply-chain vendor-screening segment and explains why exposure is acceptable.
Provide the underlying policy/control mapping showing certification is permitted with disclosure alone for an exposed named use case.
specific_concerns: The provided policy text says rollout controls and monitoring do not cure disclosure obligations when the affected segment remains exposed.
The actor summary admits the supply-chain vendor-screening segment remains exposed and below target on sanctions-risk explanation.
The available risk-acceptance draft is described as unapproved and not addressing the exposed segment, so it cannot satisfy the policy exception as stated.
The packet appears supportable only if explicit disclosure is actually included before launch, but no admissible evidence of that disclosure artifact is provided in the summary-only record.
Public governance guidance is contextual support for disclosure/monitoring practice, not direct evidence that this launch decision satisfies the internal policy threshold.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the available record, rather than only potentially compliant if explicit pre-launch disclosure is actually completed.
That monitoring, rollback, and a 6% rollout materially mitigate the weakness for compliance purposes while the affected use case remains exposed.
That the cited public guidance independently closes the internal policy gap.
